To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a novel large deletion in the mitochondrial DNA in a 13 months old infant with Pearson syndrome.
we identified a novel large deletion (4,734 bp) of the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNAs) in an infant with chronic liver dysfunction, anemic lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly.
we have identified a novel large deletion in the mtDNA in an infant with PS, and this deletion was negative in parents and elder brother.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the importance of considering PS in patients with intractable hepatomegaly and anemia, the importance of appropriate choosing of the relevant genetic tools in diagnosis, and the significance of long-term follow-up for patients with PS.

the clinical and laboratory presentations of PS, the identification of a novel mtDNA large deletion and the importance of mtDNA analysis in the etiologic diagnosis of patients with intractable liver dysfunction, anemic and lactic acidemia.

the importance of mtDNA deletion as a genetic basis of PS, and also the significance of mtDNA analysis as an essential step in the genetic evaluation of patients with intractable liver disease, anemia and/or lactic acidosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient suffered from PS, and the novel large deletion of mtDNA was the underlying cause.
the novel large deletion of 4734bp in the mtDNA is the cause of the infant’s clinical presentation.
this is a case of PS caused by novel mtDNA deletion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mtDNA deletion of the patient was a novel variant of PS, and the clinical manifestations of PS were variable, which might be related with the different sizes of the mtDNA deletion.
a novel mtDNA mutation was identified in an infant with PS, and it might be helpful to the clinical geneticists in the future.
the mtDNA deletion is the cause of this infant’s disease, and the deletion is novel.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mitochondrial disorders should be considered when patients present with intractable liver dysfunction, hepatomegaly and anemia, and that the appropriate choice of genetic testing can help identify the genetic cause of the disease.
the novel large deletion of mtDNA in the infant with PS should be identified by the multiplex ligation- dependent probe amplification assay.

mitochondrial DNA deletion can be a rare cause of intractable anemias, liver dysfunctions and lactic acidosises, especially in infants, and that the mitochondrial DNA deletion can also be a rare cause in the etiology of liver dysfunctions in children, which can be identified by multiplex ligation- dependent probe amplification assay.
